stem:
Arjun writes $216=2^{3}\times 3^{3}$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $216$ is a perfect cube with no need to group its prime factors in threes.
The cube root produces the prime factorisation $2^{3}\times 3^{3}$, rather than reading one factor from each triplet.
$216$ is a perfect cube and its cube root is $2\times 3=6$.
The same triplet test also settles every even number, not only perfect-cube checks.

teacher.key_rationale: Prime factors in complete triplets show 216 is a perfect cube; one factor from each triplet gives cube root 2×3=6. Skipping the triplet grouping, reversing root and factorisation, or widening the test to every even number all miss that hinge.
